note: Core decisions are the ones a competent session cannot avoid noticing. Depth decisions are the ones only a thorough interrogation reaches; they are where the tool either becomes safe or merely stops erroring.

materialDecisions.summary: What happens when a target name already exists: refuse the whole run, skip that file, overwrite it, or pick a different name.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: It is the difference between a failed run and a lost photo, and the user's answer forbids two of the obvious options.

materialDecisions.summary: Whether a run that cannot complete leaves nothing changed, or applies what it can.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: The reported complaint is a half-renamed directory; a fix that only improves the error message does not address it.
materialDecisions.repositoryHint: README.md describes the partial-application behavior and src/rename.js shows renameSync applied in a loop.

materialDecisions.summary: Whether files that already match the target naming scheme are included in the rename set.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: With the current plan an existing photo-001.jpg is both a rename source and a collision target, which is how the reported failure is produced.

materialDecisions.summary: How to handle a target that is occupied now but will itself be renamed later in the same run.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: Refusing every occupied target rejects runs that are actually valid; allowing them without ordering or staging corrupts data. The plan in src/rename.js has no ordering at all.

materialDecisions.summary: What a second identical run does.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: README.md states people frequently run it twice by mistake, and renumbering on the second pass silently reorders a library.

materialDecisions.summary: Whether a rename that differs only in letter case counts as a clash or a no-op on a case-insensitive filesystem.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: On Windows and macOS the existence check and the rename disagree, so a naive clash test either blocks valid renames or silently overwrites.

materialDecisions.summary: What a refused run reports, on which stream, and with what exit code.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: The user's stated need after a failure is knowing exactly what did not change; a bare non-zero exit does not provide it.
materialDecisions.repositoryHint: AGENTS.md fixes the stdout and stderr convention, so only the content and exit code are open.

materialDecisions.summary: Whether a preview or confirmation step is part of the fix, and whether safety may depend on the operator reading it.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: A preview is the tempting answer and the user explicitly refuses it as the whole fix, so a session that stops there has solved the wrong problem.

forbiddenQuestions.summary: Asking whether subdirectories should be included.
forbiddenQuestions.provedBy: src/match.js states it is deliberately not recursive and reads a single directory.

forbiddenQuestions.summary: Asking which glob or pattern syntax to support.
forbiddenQuestions.provedBy: src/match.js states that * is the only supported wildcard.

forbiddenQuestions.summary: Asking whether to add undo or a rename journal.
forbiddenQuestions.provedBy: README.md records the 1.1 decision against it and marks it out of scope.

forbiddenQuestions.summary: Asking whether output belongs on stdout or stderr.
forbiddenQuestions.provedBy: AGENTS.md fixes user-facing output to stdout and diagnostics to stderr.

forbiddenQuestions.summary: Asking whether a glob or filesystem helper library may be added.
forbiddenQuestions.provedBy: AGENTS.md bans dependencies, naming glob libraries.

forbiddenQuestions.summary: Asking how to run the tests.
forbiddenQuestions.provedBy: package.json scripts.test and AGENTS.md both state node --test.

mustPreserve: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr
mustAchieve: a run that cannot complete leaves every file unchanged
no existing file is ever overwritten
